instructions: Markdown adaptation of the organizer-provided templates. No Confluence/Jira access or approval is implied.
Keep business requirements separate from assumptions. Number functional requirements FR-1, FR-2 and trace business requirements to FR, endpoints and acceptance tests.
Use supplied headings with nonempty content. A non-applicable section must state why. Unknown owners, approval, URLs, measured load/RTO and credentials remain explicitly unknown; never invent them.
For every endpoint in generatedApi, use a level-2 heading METHOD /path in docs/api.md and the required API sections at level 3 inside that endpoint block.

API sections cover authorization/access, headers/path/query/body, required/nullable fields/types/limits, request/response examples, successful/error HTTP codes, tables, main/exception flows and external sources.

Describe frontend-to-backend field mappings, data types/PK/FK, events/messages, validation, security, caching and non-functional limits where applicable. Preserve editable PlantUML/Mermaid sources for diagrams.

Service docs distinguish actual prod/stage/test availability, declared resource limits from measured throughput, build/deploy/env/logging/monitoring/network access. No borrowed sample infrastructure, versions or metrics.
ADR compares alternatives, pros/cons, the chosen decision and consequences; status must reflect reality. Do not invent stakeholder approval.
User guide/runbook describe the generated product, not the Python platform. The product backend is C#/.NET 10 and has its own database.
Do not generate a successful test/security report. The pipeline packages its actual validation report separately as reports/validation.json.
